5Diagnostic criteria
Defining criteria: delirium Attention – attention and awareness disturbed · Onset – over a short time (usually hours to a few days), a change from baseline, tending to fluctuate during the day · Cognition – an additional disturbance: memory, disorientation, language, visuospatial ability or perception · Exclusion – not better explained by a preexisting, established or evolving neurocognitive disorder, and not in severely reduced arousal such as coma · Cause – evidence of a medical condition, substance intoxication or withdrawal, medication, toxin, or several
Bedside screenAcute onset with a fluctuating course and inattention are both required, plus either disorganized thinking or an altered level of consciousness. Timing chart: against dementia and psychosis

Defining rules
DisorderRule
Oppositional defiant disorder4 or more symptoms for 6 months, with someone other than a sibling; under 5 most days, 5 or older at least weekly
Conduct disorder3 or more in 12 months, from aggression, destruction, deceit or theft, serious rule violations
Intermittent explosive disorderVerbal aggression on average twice a week for 3 months, or 3 destructive outbursts in 12 months; age 6 or older
Disruptive mood dysregulation disorderOutbursts 3 or more a week, irritable between, in 2 or more settings, 12 months or more without a 3-month gap
PrecedenceWhen disruptive mood dysregulation disorder is met, do not also diagnose oppositional defiant or intermittent explosive disorder
